article_title: Beyond Curriculum Adoption: What District Leaders Are Saying about Using Illustrative Mathematics
citation: Hannan, M., Rainier, S., & Perry, R. (2026). Beyond curriculum adoption: What district leaders are saying about using Illustrative Mathematics. WestEd. https://www.wested.org
title: The implementation chain: HQIM implementation as a phased, multi-level, multi-year system process
description: This report frames HQIM implementation through CCSSO's "implementation chain," in which coordinated actions must occur across levels of the education system, where "each level is responsible for creating coherence for the next level" (2025, p. 8). CCSSO's analysis proposes five phases unfolding over 4 or more years: exploration, program installation, initial implementation, consistent implementation, and innovation and sustainability. The report uses this framework to organize district leaders' accounts of IM implementation as an ongoing, cyclical process rather than a one-time adoption event.
requirements: Successful HQIM uptake necessitates coordinated, integrated actions across the levels of the school system
constraints: The report states the duration of the phases is likely variable between contexts and curricula and can vary from school to school within a district
target_learning_goals: Consistent, coherent use of adopted high-quality instructional materials in mathematics
examples: The report's five interview themes are organized to reflect implementation as a cyclical process, from vision-setting through equity refinement
key_sources: Hannan, M., Rainier, S., & Perry, R. (2026). Beyond curriculum adoption: What district leaders are saying about using Illustrative Mathematics. WestEd. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED681318

article_title: Measuring What Matters: Considerations for Measuring the Implementation of High-Quality Instructional Materials in Mathematics
citation: Perry, R., Nucci, D., Walters, K., McKinney, D., Nielsen, S., & Hannan, M. (2026). Measuring what matters: Considerations for measuring the implementation of high-quality instructional materials in mathematics. WestEd. https://www.wested.org
title: Tri-annual teacher survey operationalizing dosage, adherence, instructional quality, and support
description: A teacher self-report survey administered "three times annually during the 2024–2027 study period" to all participating grades 6–8 teachers, designed to take no longer than 30 minutes per administration. The team chose self-reporting as "the least burdensome and most reliable strategy" given the logistical and fiscal challenges of direct observation in a national study. Items are drawn where possible from nationally validated surveys and operationalize dosage (units taught, percentage of class time using the core curriculum), adherence (skipping, supplementing, modifying), instructional quality (frequency of teacher and student instructional practices), and support (professional learning hours, usefulness ratings, and planning collaboration).
requirements: Requires teacher self-report items from nationally validated surveys and aggregation of responses to create individual implementation measures comparable across districts using different programs
constraints: The report acknowledges the challenges related to the reliability of self-report data and notes locally gathered fidelity data cannot be relied on because districts use different programs and measures
target_learners: grades 6–8 mathematics teachers in participating districts
target_learning_goals: measuring curriculum dosage, adherence, instructional quality, and professional learning support for impact models
examples: The survey replicates a 2018 National Survey of Science and Mathematics Education adherence question with options from Not at all to To a great extent, used to create a single adherence score with low, moderate, and high cut scores
key_sources: Perry, R., Nucci, D., Walters, K., McKinney, D., Nielsen, S., & Hannan, M. (2026). Measuring what matters: Considerations for measuring the implementation of high-quality instructional materials in mathematics. WestEd. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED681340

article_title: Measuring What Matters: Considerations for Measuring the Implementation of High-Quality Instructional Materials in Mathematics
citation: Perry, R., Nucci, D., Walters, K., McKinney, D., Nielsen, S., & Hannan, M. (2026). Measuring what matters: Considerations for measuring the implementation of high-quality instructional materials in mathematics. WestEd. https://www.wested.org
title: Short student survey measuring mathematical experiences, sense of belonging, and mathematics self-efficacy
description: A student-facing instrument, taking "no longer than 15 minutes to complete," administered at the beginning and end of each school year to triangulate teacher self-reports of implementation. It uses the same construct categories as the teacher survey—coherence, cognitive demand, collaboration and discourse, formative assessment, and differentiation—with items drawn from existing valid and reliable instruments. It includes belonging items, described as a significant predictor of motivation, and "Nine additional survey items were also included to replicate a reliable self-efficacy scale." The team plans exploratory factor analysis and correlation plots to compare teacher and student reports.
requirements: Requires items drawn from existing valid and reliable survey instruments and administration at the beginning and end of each school year
constraints: The report notes classroom practice may not meet a coherence standard for implementation fidelity if teachers' and students' reports differ, which is why student-facing instruments were created
target_learning_goals: capturing student experience of mathematical opportunities to learn and classroom interactions
examples: Illustrative Mathematics provides a Building a Mathematical Community Plan with student prompts and ways to make student thinking visible, an example of curriculum features aimed at belonging and self-efficacy
